raw_response:
This year I plan to keep doing what worked last year with some small changes. Let me think it through.

My main ground is 4 mu in the cabbage-chili rotation — chili goes in around late April, I pull it out in August, then I put cabbage straight after for the autumn crop. That's been my bread and butter for years. The other 2 mu I keep split: 1 mu eggplant and 1 mu kidney bean, next to the house where I can watch them closer.

**Chili (spring-summer, 4 mu):** I'll use hybrid seedlings from the dealer in town — the long green type sells better at Handan market. Chili is a hungry crop. I put down about 3 bags (150 kg) of compound 15-15-15 as base fertilizer per mu, then side-dress urea twice when the fruits start setting. That works out to around 20 kg N, 12 kg P, 20 kg K per mu. Well water, I run it maybe 7 times across the season — chili wilts fast in June heat. Pests are the headache — aphids, thrips, anthracnose — I spray roughly 7 times. Last year I got about 2800 kg/mu, same target this year.

**Cabbage (autumn, 4 mu):** After chili comes out, I plough the land once, not just rotary, because the chili roots are tough. Hybrid cabbage seed, the flat-headed type keeps better. Base fertilizer 2.5 bags compound plus some chicken manure I get cheap from the nearby farm. About 18 kg N, 10 kg P, 15 kg K per mu, topdress urea once at heading. Irrigate 5 times. Spray 5 times — mainly for cabbage worms and diamondback moth. Expect around 5000 kg/mu.

**Eggplant (1 mu):** Long purple hybrid, same as last year. Eggplant keeps producing all summer if you feed it. Heavy base of manure plus 2 bags compound, then urea every 20 days. Around 22 kg N, 12 kg P, 22 kg K. Irrigate 8 times, spray 6 times. Target 4000 kg.

**Kidney bean (1 mu):** Beans make their own nitrogen so I don't waste urea on them. Just 1.5 bags compound per mu. Irrigate 5 times. Only 4 sprays — beans get bean fly but otherwise cleaner than chili. Improved seed, target 2000 kg.

I'm not changing much because last year paid the school fees and left something over. Fertilizer prices are up a bit this year so I'm sticking close to my usual rates, not cutting.
